answer: One concrete defense is resource-anchored identity. Each agent runs a haven, holding a unique encrypted shard in the storage lagoon and answering random retrieval probes. Honest agents keep their shard available, earning weight via uptime and proofs. A sybil is hollow: it cannot prove data it never stored, so hollow identities lose weight and rewards. Since distinct shards cannot be pooled across keys, N fake agents need N separate storage and bandwidth commitments online all epoch. Cost scales with real resources, not free keys, making hollow identities the sybil's costliest move.
